title: Plug-in solar is coming. Plug-in batteries should follow.
excerpt: Plug-in batteries could help millions more households access the bill-saving benefits of home energy storage. With plug-in solar now on the way, Regen argues that the government should make plug-in batteries next.
content_html:
Plug-in batteries could significantly reduce household electricity bills, particularly for renters, flat dwellers and low-income households, who are largely excluded from installing traditional home battery systems today. The government has already announced regulation changes to make plug-in solar panels available as part of its response to the rise in energy costs caused by the US war with Iran. In this blog, Regen argues they should go one step further and make standalone plug-in batteries available too.

‍

The Windfall Battery is a plug-in option designed for flats and renters by London-based start-up Windfall Energy Ltd

Plug-in batteries: putting power in people’s hands

Rooftop solar and home battery systems are a well-established pillar of the government’s net zero and energy security strategy. But to date, systems that can be plugged into a regular wall socket have not been legal in Great Britain. This is in stark contrast to mainland Europe, where plug-in systems are commonplace and can be bought off the shelf from Ikea or Lidl.

Plug-in solar has been available for almost a decade in Germany, where there are now more than a million systems in place. In March this year, the UK government announced regulation changes to make plug-in solar panels available ‘within months’, as part of its response to the rise in energy costs caused by the US war in Iran. However, the announcement was noticeably quiet on plug-in batteries.

In this insight piece, we discuss:

  • What a plug-in battery is and how they work
  • How much households could save
  • Who would benefit (spoiler, it’s those currently cut out from the benefits of home batteries)
  • The wider energy system benefits
  • The next steps for government on safety and regulation.

‍

What is a plug-in battery and how does it work?

A plug-in battery is a portable energy storage unit that can be plugged into a standard wall socket without any modification to the household wiring. It charges by drawing electricity through the socket – typically during the off-peak period of a time-of-use tariff – and discharges back through the same socket to offset household demand at times when electricity is more expensive.

Unlike traditional domestic battery systems, which must be hardwired into the home’s electrical system by a qualified electrician, plug-in batteries can be bought off the shelf and plugged into a wall socket like any other household appliance.

‍

‍

This removes the need for professional installation and significantly reduces the cost compared to a traditional system. Typically around £1,000 to 1,500 of the total cost of a professionally installed home battery is for installation. This cost component doesn’t scale directly with storage capacity, so small systems have a very high cost per kWh. Conversely, unit costs of plug-in systems are very low.

‍

‍

‍

How much could households save with a plug-in battery?

A battery paired with a time-of-use tariff lets households charge when electricity is cheap and discharge when it is expensive. The household saves money overall when the bill reduction over the battery’s lifetime exceeds its upfront cost.

The charts below show Regen’s analysis of cumulative energy spend over 10 years for low-, medium- and high-energy households, comparing two scenarios: a single 3 kWh plug-in battery on the Octopus Go time-of-use tariff against the same household with no battery on a flat-rate tariff. In each case, the battery pays back from around 2.5 years onwards, with 10-year savings reaching up to £2,400 for the high-energy household.

‍

‍

Whether a plug-in battery saves money depends on several factors, including the choice of tariff, the battery size and the extent to which other household demand falls in off-peak periods of a time-of-use tariff. Figure 2 shows cumulative energy spend over 10 years, with and without a battery. The shaded band shows the range of outcomes across different battery sizes and proportions of demand falling in daytime higher-priced periods. Households that can shift demand to off-peak periods and utilise larger, or multiple, batteries could reduce their total costs over 10 years by 30-34%.

‍

‍

Caveat: for this analysis we have assumed no change in electricity tariffs. While this is unlikely, there is little consensus on the direction of future electricity prices. If tariffs increase, savings from purchasing a battery are likely to be greater.

‍

Who benefits?

Plug-in batteries are low-cost, require no permission to install and can be removed and taken to the next home. This means they can extend the benefits of batteries and smart tariff arbitrage to a range of consumer groups and home types that are currently excluded from the market for traditional home battery systems.

These include:

  • The 9 million rented households in Great Britain who typically cannot make structural modifications to their property
  • The c. 6 million flat and apartment households who often lack the space required for a professionally installed unit
  • Low-income households, for whom the combined hardware and installation cost of a fixed system remains out of reach. 11.4m households are in the bottom 40% of incomes.

After accounting for overlap, these households represent in the order of 12 to 14 million households, or close to half of all households in Great Britain. Plug-in batteries would enable a much wider share of the country to feel the energy transition includes them, extending its benefits and sense of belonging well beyond more affluent owner-occupiers.

Energy system benefits

In addition to the bill reductions for households that purchase them, plug-in battery systems can deliver system-wide benefits. Under a rapid uptake scenario, by 2030 the total discharge capacity could reach almost a gigawatt and storage capacity over 4 GWh.

The Clean Flexibility Roadmap sets out a target of 23-27 GW of short-duration storage capacity by 2030. Starting from a position in 2026 with no installations, even with rapid uptake plug-in batteries would contribute a small portion of that 2030 target.

Plug-in batteries also won’t provide the full range of system services that larger battery systems can provide, such as frequency response, inertia or reactive power. If the 800 W discharge limit applied to plug-in solar is mirrored for batteries, the flexibility each unit can offer will be modest.

However, with the right tariffs and incentives, in the longer term they could provide an important contribution to peak demand reduction (lowering the cost of meeting demand, supporting capacity adequacy and avoiding network constraints) and supporting the integration of variable renewable generation. These benefits flow to all electricity consumers, not just those who own a battery, by lowering the costs that ultimately end up in everyone’s bills.

‍

‍

‍

Many consumers would likely buy these alongside plug-in solar panels. Pairing the two brings added system benefits: it dampens the adverse impacts of plug-in solar (correlated generation on sunny summer days can lead to voltage rise on the distribution networks and challenges with low levels of demand on the transmission system) while also letting households capture higher value by using the power later in the day.

Plug-in batteries would also provide a level of household resilience by providing enough power to keep essential devices running power during power cuts. As 800 W is not enough to run an oven, households would still feel the impact of an outage, but it would be sufficient to power essentials like lights, Wi-Fi, and phones.  

Safety and regulation

The reason plug-in batteries are not yet available in Great Britain is that existing wiring regulations were not designed for appliances to discharge power back into the household circuit. BS 7671, which governs electrical installations in UK homes, does not currently permit it.

Household wiring is protected from overheating and fire by circuit breakers in the consumer unit (the fuse board). Each circuit’s breaker has a lower rating than the wiring’s actual thermal limit, providing a safety margin. A ring main is typically protected by a 32 A circuit breaker (equivalent to 7.4 kW at standard UK voltage) and 20 A circuit breaker is used for radial circuits.

The problem with a discharging battery is known as load masking. Circuit breakers only detect the current flowing past them from the consumer unit and they cannot ‘see’ that a battery is plugged in. So when a battery discharges into a wall socket, the appliances on that circuit can draw power from the battery instead of the consumer unit – and the breaker continues to allow current up to its rating on top of what the battery is supplying. The wiring closest to the appliances can therefore carry more current than the circuit breaker is set to protect against. Exceeding the rated current could lead to the wire getting hot, increasing the risk of a fire. This is illustrated in the diagram below:

‍

‍

Capping plug-in devices at 800 W, as BS 7671 Amendment 4 does for plug-in solar, keeps the extra contribution small enough that this is unlikely to push the wiring beyond safe limits. The same regulatory barrier did apply to plug-in solar until March 2026, when DESNZ committed to change the regulations following a safety study carried out by Arceio. BS 7671 Amendment 4, published in April 2026, now provides the wiring regulation foundation for plug-in solar; a BSI product standard is expected by mid-2026.

A separate safety consideration is the risk of fire from the battery itself. For installed home batteries, this is addressed by PAS 63100:2024, which sets out fire safety requirements including separation from living spaces, ventilation and detection. These rules cannot translate directly to a portable plug-in device, so a plug-in framework would need to draw on product-level safety standards appropriate to domestic use.

Next steps for the government

It’s clear that plug-in batteries could be transformational for households in Great Britain that to date have been excluded from the benefits of home batteries. It’s positive that the government has announced plug-in solar, but it has left plug-in batteries in a grey area.

Regen suggests that DESNZ should now:

  • Commit to a date by which plug-in batteries will be legally available for use in Great Britain
  • Commission a rapid safety study for plug-in batteries, and work with the IET and BSI to update BS 7671 (the UK wiring regulations) accordingly
  • Sponsor a new product safety standard through BSI for battery fire safety in portable in-home devices (distinct from the PAS 63100 framework written for installed systems).

With the government commitment to cutting £300 from household energy bills looking increasingly out of reach, introducing a new product to the market that delivers meaningful bill savings at no cost to the Treasury should be one of the easier calls to make.

sentences.en: The household saves money overall when the bill reduction over the battery’s lifetime exceeds its upfront cost.
sentences.zh: 当电池使用寿命期间的费用减少超过其前期成本时，家庭总体上可以节省资金。

blocks.html_en: The charts below show Regen’s analysis of cumulative energy spend over 10 years for low-, medium- and high-energy households, comparing two scenarios: a single 3 kWh plug-in battery on the Octopus Go time-of-use tariff against the same household with no battery on a flat-rate tariff. In each case, the battery pays back from around 2.5 years onwards, with 10-year savings reaching up to £2,400 for the high-energy household.

sentences.en: The charts below show Regen’s analysis of cumulative energy spend over 10 years for low-, medium- and high-energy households, comparing two scenarios: a single 3 kWh plug-in battery on the Octopus Go time-of-use tariff against the same household with no battery on a flat-rate tariff.
sentences.zh: 下图显示了 Regen 对低、中和高能耗家庭 10 年来累计能源消耗的分析，比较了两种情况：使用 Octopus Go 的单个 3 kWh 插入式电池的分时电价与没有电池的统一电价的同一家庭。

sentences.en: In each case, the battery pays back from around 2.5 years onwards, with 10-year savings reaching up to £2,400 for the high-energy household.
sentences.zh: 在每种情况下，电池从大约 2.5 年起即可收回成本，10 年可为高能耗家庭节省高达 2,400 英镑。

sentences.en: Cumulative energy spends for low-, medium- and high-energy households.
sentences.zh: 低、中、高能源家庭的累计能源支出。

sentences.en: A low-energy household may be a flat or one-bedroom house and a high-energy household represents homes with four to five bedrooms and occupants.
sentences.zh: 低能耗家庭可能是公寓或一卧室房屋，高能耗家庭代表有四到五间卧室和居住者的房屋。

sentences.en: Typical consumption values from Ofgem were used and it was assumed only one 3 kWh plug-in battery was installed for each case (Ofgem, 2026).
sentences.zh: 使用 Ofgem 的典型消耗值，并假设每种情况仅安装一个 3 kWh 插入式电池（Ofgem，2026）。

blocks.html_en: Whether a plug-in battery saves money depends on several factors, including the choice of tariff, the battery size and the extent to which other household demand falls in off-peak periods of a time-of-use tariff. Figure 2 shows cumulative energy spend over 10 years, with and without a battery. The shaded band shows the range of outcomes across different battery sizes and proportions of demand falling in daytime higher-priced periods. Households that can shift demand to off-peak periods and utilise larger, or multiple, batteries could reduce their total costs over 10 years by 30-34%.

sentences.en: Whether a plug-in battery saves money depends on several factors, including the choice of tariff, the battery size and the extent to which other household demand falls in off-peak periods of a time-of-use tariff.
sentences.zh: 插入式电池是否省钱取决于几个因素，包括电价选择、电池尺寸以及分时电价非高峰时段其他家庭需求下降的程度。

sentences.en: Figure 2 shows cumulative energy spend over 10 years, with and without a battery.
sentences.zh: 图 2 显示了 10 年来的累计能源消耗（有电池和无电池）。

sentences.en: The shaded band shows the range of outcomes across different battery sizes and proportions of demand falling in daytime higher-priced periods.
sentences.zh: 阴影带显示了不同电池尺寸的结果范围以及白天高价时段需求下降的比例。

sentences.en: Households that can shift demand to off-peak periods and utilise larger, or multiple, batteries could reduce their total costs over 10 years by 30-34%.
sentences.zh: 能够将需求转移到非高峰时段并使用更大或多块电池的家庭可以在 10 年内将总成本降低 30-34%。

sentences.en: Cumulative energy spends for a range of battery and energy usage pattern configurations.
sentences.zh: 一系列电池和能源使用模式配置的累计能源支出。

sentences.en: Values are based on the Octopus Go time-of-use tariff and assume a ypical medium-energy two to three-bedroom household.
sentences.zh: 数值基于 Octopus Go 的分时电价，并假设为典型的中等能耗的两居室至三居室家庭。

blocks.html_en: Caveat: for this analysis we have assumed no change in electricity tariffs. While this is unlikely, there is little consensus on the direction of future electricity prices. If tariffs increase, savings from purchasing a battery are likely to be greater.

sentences.en: Caveat: for this analysis we have assumed no change in electricity tariffs.
sentences.zh: 注意：在本分析中，我们假设电价没有变化。

sentences.en: While this is unlikely, there is little consensus on the direction of future electricity prices.
sentences.zh: 虽然这种情况不太可能发生，但人们对未来电价的走向几乎没有达成共识。

sentences.en: If tariffs increase, savings from purchasing a battery are likely to be greater.
sentences.zh: 如果关税增加，购买电池所节省的费用可能会更大。

blocks.html_en: Who benefits?

sentences.en: Who benefits?
sentences.zh: 谁受益？

blocks.html_en: Plug-in batteries are low-cost, require no permission to install and can be removed and taken to the next home. This means they can extend the benefits of batteries and smart tariff arbitrage to a range of consumer groups and home types that are currently excluded from the market for traditional home battery systems.

sentences.en: Plug-in batteries are low-cost, require no permission to install and can be removed and taken to the next home.
sentences.zh: 插入式电池成本低廉，无需安装许可，并且可以拆卸并带到下一个家。

sentences.en: This means they can extend the benefits of batteries and smart tariff arbitrage to a range of consumer groups and home types that are currently excluded from the market for traditional home battery systems.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们可以将电池和智能关税套利的好处扩展到目前被排除在传统家用电池系统市场之外的一系列消费者群体和家庭类型。

blocks.html_en: These include:

sentences.en: These include:
sentences.zh: 这些包括：

blocks.html_en: • The 9 million rented households in Great Britain who typically cannot make structural modifications to their property

sentences.en: The 9 million rented households in Great Britain who typically cannot make structural modifications to their property
sentences.zh: 英国 900 万出租家庭通常无法对其房产进行结构性改造

blocks.html_en: • The c. 6 million flat and apartment households who often lack the space required for a professionally installed unit

sentences.en: The c.
sentences.zh: c.

sentences.en: 6 million flat and apartment households who often lack the space required for a professionally installed unit
sentences.zh: 600 万公寓和公寓家庭往往缺乏专业安装单元所需的空间

blocks.html_en: • Low-income households, for whom the combined hardware and installation cost of a fixed system remains out of reach. 11.4m households are in the bottom 40% of incomes.

sentences.en: Low-income households, for whom the combined hardware and installation cost of a fixed system remains out of reach.
sentences.zh: 对于低收入家庭来说，固定系统的硬件和安装总成本仍然遥不可及。

sentences.en: 11.4m households are in the bottom 40% of incomes.
sentences.zh: 1140万户家庭处于收入最底层的40%。

blocks.html_en: After accounting for overlap, these households represent in the order of 12 to 14 million households, or close to half of all households in Great Britain. Plug-in batteries would enable a much wider share of the country to feel the energy transition includes them, extending its benefits and sense of belonging well beyond more affluent owner-occupiers.

sentences.en: After accounting for overlap, these households represent in the order of 12 to 14 million households, or close to half of all households in Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 考虑到重叠因素后，这些家庭数量约为 12 至 1400 万户，接近英国所有家庭的一半。

sentences.en: Plug-in batteries would enable a much wider share of the country to feel the energy transition includes them, extending its benefits and sense of belonging well beyond more affluent owner-occupiers.
sentences.zh: 插电式电池将使该国更广泛的地区感受到能源转型包括它们，将其好处和归属感远远超出更富裕的自住业主。

blocks.html_en: Energy system benefits

sentences.en: Energy system benefits
sentences.zh: 能源系统的好处

blocks.html_en: In addition to the bill reductions for households that purchase them, plug-in battery systems can deliver system-wide benefits. Under a rapid uptake scenario, by 2030 the total discharge capacity could reach almost a gigawatt and storage capacity over 4 GWh.

sentences.en: In addition to the bill reductions for households that purchase them, plug-in battery systems can deliver system-wide benefits.
sentences.zh: 除了减少购买电池系统的家庭的费用外，插入式电池系统还可以带来全系统的好处。

sentences.en: Under a rapid uptake scenario, by 2030 the total discharge capacity could reach almost a gigawatt and storage capacity over 4 GWh.
sentences.zh: 在快速吸收的情况下，到 2030 年，总放电容量将达到近 1 吉瓦，存储容量将超过 4 GWh。

blocks.html_en: The Clean Flexibility Roadmap sets out a target of 23-27 GW of short-duration storage capacity by 2030. Starting from a position in 2026 with no installations, even with rapid uptake plug-in batteries would contribute a small portion of that 2030 target.

sentences.en: The Clean Flexibility Roadmap sets out a target of 23-27 GW of short-duration storage capacity by 2030.
sentences.zh: 清洁灵活性路线图设定了到 2030 年短期存储容量达到 23-27 吉瓦的目标。

sentences.en: Starting from a position in 2026 with no installations, even with rapid uptake plug-in batteries would contribute a small portion of that 2030 target.
sentences.zh: 从 2026 年没有安装的情况开始，即使快速采用插入式电池，也只能为 2030 年目标贡献一小部分。

blocks.html_en: Plug-in batteries also won’t provide the full range of system services that larger battery systems can provide, such as frequency response, inertia or reactive power. If the 800 W discharge limit applied to plug-in solar is mirrored for batteries, the flexibility each unit can offer will be modest.

sentences.en: Plug-in batteries also won’t provide the full range of system services that larger battery systems can provide, such as frequency response, inertia or reactive power.
sentences.zh: 插入式电池也无法提供大型电池系统可以提供的全方位系统服务，例如频率响应、惯性或无功功率。

sentences.en: If the 800 W discharge limit applied to plug-in solar is mirrored for batteries, the flexibility each unit can offer will be modest.
sentences.zh: 如果适用于插入式太阳能的 800 W 放电限制也适用于电池，那么每个单元所能提供的灵活性将是适度的。

blocks.html_en: However, with the right tariffs and incentives, in the longer term they could provide an important contribution to peak demand reduction (lowering the cost of meeting demand, supporting capacity adequacy and avoiding network constraints) and supporting the integration of variable renewable generation. These benefits flow to all electricity consumers, not just those who own a battery, by lowering the costs that ultimately end up in everyone’s bills.

sentences.en: However, with the right tariffs and incentives, in the longer term they could provide an important contribution to peak demand reduction (lowering the cost of meeting demand, supporting capacity adequacy and avoiding network constraints) and supporting the integration of variable renewable generation.
sentences.zh: 然而，通过适当的关税和激励措施，从长远来看，它们可以为减少峰值需求（降低满足需求的成本，支持容量充足性并避免网络限制）和支持可变可再生能源发电的整合做出重要贡献。

sentences.en: These benefits flow to all electricity consumers, not just those who own a battery, by lowering the costs that ultimately end up in everyone’s bills.
sentences.zh: 通过降低最终影响每个人账单的成本，这些好处惠及所有电力消费者，而不仅仅是那些拥有电池的人。

sentences.en: Chart shows the range between two illustrative GB-wide uptake scenarios for plug-in batteries developed by Regen.
sentences.zh: 图表显示了 Regen 开发的插入式电池的两种说明性的全英国使用场景之间的范围。

sentences.en: Assumptions for rapid scenario: 800 W discharge capacity, average 4 kWh storage capacity, uptake per year reaches 500,000 by 2030.
sentences.zh: 快速情景假设：放电容量800瓦，平均存储容量4千瓦时，到2030年每年吸收量达到50万个。

sentences.en: Assumptions for slow scenario: 800 W discharge capacity, average 2 kWh storage capacity, uptake per year reaches 150,000 by 2031.
sentences.zh: 慢速场景假设：放电容量800瓦，平均存储容量2千瓦时，到2031年每年吸收量达到15万个。

blocks.html_en: Many consumers would likely buy these alongside plug-in solar panels. Pairing the two brings added system benefits: it dampens the adverse impacts of plug-in solar (correlated generation on sunny summer days can lead to voltage rise on the distribution networks and challenges with low levels of demand on the transmission system) while also letting households capture higher value by using the power later in the day.

sentences.en: Many consumers would likely buy these alongside plug-in solar panels.
sentences.zh: 许多消费者可能会与插入式太阳能电池板一起购买这些产品。

sentences.en: Pairing the two brings added system benefits: it dampens the adverse impacts of plug-in solar (correlated generation on sunny summer days can lead to voltage rise on the distribution networks and challenges with low levels of demand on the transmission system) while also letting households capture higher value by using the power later in the day.
sentences.zh: 将两者结合起来会带来额外的系统优势：它可以减轻插入式太阳能的不利影响（阳光明媚的夏日关联发电可能会导致配电网络电压上升，并对输电系统的需求水平较低带来挑战），同时还可以让家庭通过在当天晚些时候使用电力来获得更高的价值。

blocks.html_en: Plug-in batteries would also provide a level of household resilience by providing enough power to keep essential devices running power during power cuts. As 800 W is not enough to run an oven, households would still feel the impact of an outage, but it would be sufficient to power essentials like lights, Wi-Fi, and phones.

sentences.en: Plug-in batteries would also provide a level of household resilience by providing enough power to keep essential devices running power during power cuts.
sentences.zh: 插入式电池还可以在断电期间提供足够的电力来保持基本设备的供电，从而提供一定程度的家庭弹性。

sentences.en: As 800 W is not enough to run an oven, households would still feel the impact of an outage, but it would be sufficient to power essentials like lights, Wi-Fi, and phones.
sentences.zh: 由于 800 瓦不足以运行烤箱，家庭仍会感受到停电的影响，但足以为灯、Wi-Fi 和电话等必需品供电。

blocks.html_en: Safety and regulation

sentences.en: Safety and regulation
sentences.zh: 安全与监管

blocks.html_en: The reason plug-in batteries are not yet available in Great Britain is that existing wiring regulations were not designed for appliances to discharge power back into the household circuit. BS 7671, which governs electrical installations in UK homes, does not currently permit it.

sentences.en: The reason plug-in batteries are not yet available in Great Britain is that existing wiring regulations were not designed for appliances to discharge power back into the household circuit.
sentences.zh: 英国尚未提供插入式电池的原因是，现有的布线法规并不是为电器将电力释放回家庭电路而设计的。

sentences.en: BS 7671, which governs electrical installations in UK homes, does not currently permit it.
sentences.zh: 管理英国家庭电气安装的 BS 7671 目前不允许这样做。

blocks.html_en: Household wiring is protected from overheating and fire by circuit breakers in the consumer unit (the fuse board). Each circuit’s breaker has a lower rating than the wiring’s actual thermal limit, providing a safety margin. A ring main is typically protected by a 32 A circuit breaker (equivalent to 7.4 kW at standard UK voltage) and 20 A circuit breaker is used for radial circuits.

sentences.en: Household wiring is protected from overheating and fire by circuit breakers in the consumer unit (the fuse board).
sentences.zh: 通过消费单元（保险丝板）中的断路器来保护家庭布线免受过热和火灾的影响。

sentences.en: Each circuit’s breaker has a lower rating than the wiring’s actual thermal limit, providing a safety margin.
sentences.zh: 每个断路器的额定值均低于接线的实际热极限，从而提供了安全裕度。

sentences.en: A ring main is typically protected by a 32 A circuit breaker (equivalent to 7.4 kW at standard UK voltage) and 20 A circuit breaker is used for radial circuits.
sentences.zh: 环形干线通常由 32 A 断路器（相当于英国标准电压下的 7.4 kW）保护，20 A 断路器用于径向电路。

blocks.html_en: The problem with a discharging battery is known as load masking. Circuit breakers only detect the current flowing past them from the consumer unit and they cannot ‘see’ that a battery is plugged in. So when a battery discharges into a wall socket, the appliances on that circuit can draw power from the battery instead of the consumer unit – and the breaker continues to allow current up to its rating on top of what the battery is supplying. The wiring closest to the appliances can therefore carry more current than the circuit breaker is set to protect against. Exceeding the rated current could lead to the wire getting hot, increasing the risk of a fire. This is illustrated in the diagram below:

sentences.en: The problem with a discharging battery is known as load masking.
sentences.zh: 电池放电的问题称为负载屏蔽。

sentences.en: Circuit breakers only detect the current flowing past them from the consumer unit and they cannot ‘see’ that a battery is plugged in.
sentences.zh: 断路器只能检测从消费单元流过它们的电流，它们无法“看到”电池是否已插入。

sentences.en: So when a battery discharges into a wall socket, the appliances on that circuit can draw power from the battery instead of the consumer unit – and the breaker continues to allow current up to its rating on top of what the battery is supplying.
sentences.zh: 因此，当电池向墙壁插座放电时，该电路上的电器可以从电池而不是消费装置获取电力，并且断路器继续允许电流达到电池供电的额定值。

sentences.en: The wiring closest to the appliances can therefore carry more current than the circuit breaker is set to protect against.
sentences.zh: 因此，最靠近设备的接线所承载的电流可能大于断路器设置的保护电流。

sentences.en: Exceeding the rated current could lead to the wire getting hot, increasing the risk of a fire.
sentences.zh: 超过额定电流可能会导致电线变热，增加火灾风险。

blocks.html_en: Capping plug-in devices at 800 W, as BS 7671 Amendment 4 does for plug-in solar, keeps the extra contribution small enough that this is unlikely to push the wiring beyond safe limits. The same regulatory barrier did apply to plug-in solar until March 2026, when DESNZ committed to change the regulations following a safety study carried out by Arceio. BS 7671 Amendment 4, published in April 2026, now provides the wiring regulation foundation for plug-in solar; a BSI product standard is expected by mid-2026.

sentences.en: Capping plug-in devices at 800 W, as BS 7671 Amendment 4 does for plug-in solar, keeps the extra contribution small enough that this is unlikely to push the wiring beyond safe limits.
sentences.zh: 正如 BS 7671 修正案 4 对插入式太阳能所做的那样，将插入式设备的功率限制在 800 W，使额外的贡献足够小，从而不太可能使接线超出安全限制。

sentences.en: The same regulatory barrier did apply to plug-in solar until March 2026, when DESNZ committed to change the regulations following a safety study carried out by Arceio.
sentences.zh: 直到 2026 年 3 月，同样的监管障碍确实适用于插电式太阳能，当时 DESNZ 承诺在 Arceio 进行安全研究后更改法规。

sentences.en: BS 7671 Amendment 4, published in April 2026, now provides the wiring regulation foundation for plug-in solar; a BSI product standard is expected by mid-2026.
sentences.zh: BS 7671修正案4于2026年4月发布，现在为插电式太阳能提供了布线法规基础； BSI 产品标准预计将于 2026 年中期制定。

blocks.html_en: A separate safety consideration is the risk of fire from the battery itself. For installed home batteries, this is addressed by PAS 63100:2024, which sets out fire safety requirements including separation from living spaces, ventilation and detection. These rules cannot translate directly to a portable plug-in device, so a plug-in framework would need to draw on product-level safety standards appropriate to domestic use.

sentences.en: A separate safety consideration is the risk of fire from the battery itself.
sentences.zh: 另一个安全考虑因素是电池本身的火灾风险。

sentences.en: For installed home batteries, this is addressed by PAS 63100:2024, which sets out fire safety requirements including separation from living spaces, ventilation and detection.
sentences.zh: 对于已安装的家用电池，PAS 63100:2024 解决了这一问题，其中规定了消防安全要求，包括与居住空间的隔离、通风和检测。

sentences.en: These rules cannot translate directly to a portable plug-in device, so a plug-in framework would need to draw on product-level safety standards appropriate to domestic use.
sentences.zh: 这些规则不能直接转化为便携式插入式设备，因此插入式框架需要借鉴适合家庭使用的产品级安全标准。

blocks.html_en: Next steps for the government

sentences.en: Next steps for the government
sentences.zh: 政府的下一步行动

blocks.html_en: It’s clear that plug-in batteries could be transformational for households in Great Britain that to date have been excluded from the benefits of home batteries. It’s positive that the government has announced plug-in solar, but it has left plug-in batteries in a grey area.

sentences.en: It’s clear that plug-in batteries could be transformational for households in Great Britain that to date have been excluded from the benefits of home batteries.
sentences.zh: 显然，插电式电池可能会给英国家庭带来变革，因为迄今为止，英国家庭仍无法享受家用电池带来的好处。

sentences.en: It’s positive that the government has announced plug-in solar, but it has left plug-in batteries in a grey area.
sentences.zh: 政府宣布推出插电式太阳能是积极的，但它却将插电式电池置于灰色地带。

blocks.html_en: Regen suggests that DESNZ should now:

sentences.en: Regen suggests that DESNZ should now:
sentences.zh: Regen 建议 DESNZ 现在应该：

blocks.html_en: • Commit to a date by which plug-in batteries will be legally available for use in Great Britain

sentences.en: Commit to a date by which plug-in batteries will be legally available for use in Great Britain
sentences.zh: 承诺插入式电池在英国合法使用的日期

blocks.html_en: • Commission a rapid safety study for plug-in batteries, and work with the IET and BSI to update BS 7671 (the UK wiring regulations) accordingly

sentences.en: Commission a rapid safety study for plug-in batteries, and work with the IET and BSI to update BS 7671 (the UK wiring regulations) accordingly
sentences.zh: 委托对插入式电池进行快速安全研究，并与 IET 和 BSI 合作相应更新 BS 7671（英国接线法规）

blocks.html_en: • Sponsor a new product safety standard through BSI for battery fire safety in portable in-home devices (distinct from the PAS 63100 framework written for installed systems).

sentences.en: Sponsor a new product safety standard through BSI for battery fire safety in portable in-home devices (distinct from the PAS 63100 framework written for installed systems).
sentences.zh: 通过 BSI 赞助便携式家用设备电池防火安全的新产品安全标准（与为安装系统编写的 PAS 63100 框架不同）。

blocks.html_en: With the government commitment to cutting £300 from household energy bills looking increasingly out of reach, introducing a new product to the market that delivers meaningful bill savings at no cost to the Treasury should be one of the easier calls to make.

sentences.en: With the government commitment to cutting £300 from household energy bills looking increasingly out of reach, introducing a new product to the market that delivers meaningful bill savings at no cost to the Treasury should be one of the easier calls to make.
sentences.zh: 由于政府承诺从家庭能源账单中削减 300 英镑看起来越来越遥不可及，因此向市场推出一种新产品，无需财政部承担任何费用即可节省大量账单，这应该是更容易做出的决定之一。

插入式电池可以显着降低家庭电费，特别是对于租房者、公寓居民和低收入家庭来说，如今他们基本上无法安装传统的家用电池系统。 作为应对美国与伊朗战争导致的能源成本上涨的一部分，政府已经宣布了监管改革，以提供插入式太阳能电池板。 在这篇博客中，Regen 认为他们应该更进一步，提供独立的插入式电池。

‍

Windfall Battery 是伦敦初创公司 Windfall Energy Ltd 为公寓和租房者设计的插件选项

插入式电池：将电力交到人们手中

屋顶太阳能和家用电池系统是政府净零排放和能源安全战略的既定支柱。 但迄今为止，可以插入普通墙壁插座的系统在英国尚未合法。 这与欧洲大陆形成鲜明对比，欧洲大陆的插入式系统很常见，可以从宜家或 Lidl 购买现成的系统。

插电式太阳能在德国已经应用了近十年，目前已经安装了超过一百万个系统。 今年三月，英国政府宣布修改法规，“在几个月内”推出插入式太阳能电池板，作为应对美国伊朗战争导致能源成本上涨的一部分。 然而，有关插电式电池的公告却明显安静。

在这篇见解文章中，我们讨论：

  • 什么是插入式电池及其工作原理
  • 家庭可以节省多少
  • 谁会受益（剧透，是那些目前无法享受家用电池好处的人）
  • 更广泛的能源系统受益
  • 政府在安全和监管方面的下一步措施。

‍

什么是插入式电池及其工作原理？

插入式电池是一种便携式能量存储单元，可以插入标准墙壁插座，无需对家庭布线进行任何修改。 它通过插座汲取电力来充电（通常是在分时电价的非高峰时段），并通过同一个插座放电，以抵消电价较高时的家庭需求。

传统的家用电池系统必须由合格的电工将其硬连线到家庭的电气系统中，而插入式电池可以直接购买，然后像任何其他家用电器一样插入墙壁插座。

‍

‍

与传统系统相比，这消除了专业安装的需要，并显着降低了成本。 通常，专业安装的家用电池的总成本约为 1,000 至 1,500 英镑用于安装。 该成本组成部分并不直接随着存储容量而扩展，因此小型系统的每千瓦时成本非常高。 相反，插件系统的单位成本非常低。

‍

‍

‍

使用插入式电池可以为家庭节省多少费用？

配备分时电价的电池可以让家庭在电价便宜时充电，在电价昂贵时放电。 当电池使用寿命期间的费用减少超过其前期成本时，家庭总体上可以节省资金。

下图显示了 Regen 对低、中和高能耗家庭 10 年来累计能源消耗的分析，比较了两种情况：使用 Octopus Go 的单个 3 kWh 插入式电池的分时电价与没有电池的统一电价的同一家庭。 在每种情况下，电池从大约 2.5 年起即可收回成本，10 年可为高能耗家庭节省高达 2,400 英镑。

‍

‍

插入式电池是否省钱取决于几个因素，包括电价选择、电池尺寸以及分时电价非高峰时段其他家庭需求下降的程度。 图 2 显示了 10 年来的累计能源消耗（有电池和无电池）。 阴影带显示了不同电池尺寸的结果范围以及白天高价时段需求下降的比例。 能够将需求转移到非高峰时段并使用更大或多块电池的家庭可以在 10 年内将总成本降低 30-34%。

‍

‍

注意：在本分析中，我们假设电价没有变化。 虽然这种情况不太可能发生，但人们对未来电价的走向几乎没有达成共识。 如果关税增加，购买电池所节省的费用可能会更大。

‍

谁受益？

插入式电池成本低廉，无需安装许可，并且可以拆卸并带到下一个家。 这意味着他们可以将电池和智能关税套利的好处扩展到目前被排除在传统家用电池系统市场之外的一系列消费者群体和家庭类型。

这些包括：

  • 英国 900 万出租家庭通常无法对其房产进行结构性改造
  • c. 600 万公寓和公寓家庭往往缺乏专业安装单元所需的空间
  • 对于低收入家庭来说，固定系统的硬件和安装总成本仍然遥不可及。 1140万户家庭处于收入最底层的40%。

考虑到重叠因素后，这些家庭数量约为 12 至 1400 万户，接近英国所有家庭的一半。 插电式电池将使该国更广泛的地区感受到能源转型包括它们，将其好处和归属感远远超出更富裕的自住业主。

能源系统的好处

除了减少购买电池系统的家庭的费用外，插入式电池系统还可以带来全系统的好处。 在快速吸收的情况下，到 2030 年，总放电容量将达到近 1 吉瓦，存储容量将超过 4 GWh。

清洁灵活性路线图设定了到 2030 年短期存储容量达到 23-27 吉瓦的目标。 从 2026 年没有安装的情况开始，即使快速采用插入式电池，也只能为 2030 年目标贡献一小部分。

插入式电池也无法提供大型电池系统可以提供的全方位系统服务，例如频率响应、惯性或无功功率。 如果适用于插入式太阳能的 800 W 放电限制也适用于电池，那么每个单元所能提供的灵活性将是适度的。

然而，通过适当的关税和激励措施，从长远来看，它们可以为减少峰值需求（降低满足需求的成本，支持容量充足性并避免网络限制）和支持可变可再生能源发电的整合做出重要贡献。 通过降低最终影响每个人账单的成本，这些好处惠及所有电力消费者，而不仅仅是那些拥有电池的人。

‍

‍

‍

许多消费者可能会与插入式太阳能电池板一起购买这些产品。 将两者结合起来会带来额外的系统优势：它可以减轻插入式太阳能的不利影响（阳光明媚的夏日关联发电可能会导致配电网络电压上升，并对输电系统的需求水平较低带来挑战），同时还可以让家庭通过在当天晚些时候使用电力来获得更高的价值。

插入式电池还可以在断电期间提供足够的电力来保持基本设备的供电，从而提供一定程度的家庭弹性。 由于 800 瓦不足以运行烤箱，家庭仍会感受到停电的影响，但足以为灯、Wi-Fi 和电话等必需品供电。

安全与监管

英国尚未提供插入式电池的原因是，现有的布线法规并不是为电器将电力释放回家庭电路而设计的。 管理英国家庭电气安装的 BS 7671 目前不允许这样做。

通过消费单元（保险丝板）中的断路器来保护家庭布线免受过热和火灾的影响。 每个断路器的额定值均低于接线的实际热极限，从而提供了安全裕度。 环形干线通常由 32 A 断路器（相当于英国标准电压下的 7.4 kW）保护，20 A 断路器用于径向电路。

电池放电的问题称为负载屏蔽。 断路器只能检测从消费单元流过它们的电流，它们无法“看到”电池是否已插入。 因此，当电池向墙壁插座放电时，该电路上的电器可以从电池而不是消费装置获取电力，并且断路器继续允许电流达到电池供电的额定值。 因此，最靠近设备的接线所承载的电流可能大于断路器设置的保护电流。 超过额定电流可能会导致电线变热，增加火灾风险。 如下图所示：

‍

‍

正如 BS 7671 修正案 4 对插入式太阳能所做的那样，将插入式设备的功率限制在 800 W，使额外的贡献足够小，从而不太可能使接线超出安全限制。 直到 2026 年 3 月，同样的监管障碍确实适用于插电式太阳能，当时 DESNZ 承诺在 Arceio 进行安全研究后更改法规。 BS 7671修正案4于2026年4月发布，现在为插电式太阳能提供了布线法规基础； BSI 产品标准预计将于 2026 年中期制定。

另一个安全考虑因素是电池本身的火灾风险。 对于已安装的家用电池，PAS 63100:2024 解决了这一问题，其中规定了消防安全要求，包括与居住空间的隔离、通风和检测。 这些规则不能直接转化为便携式插入式设备，因此插入式框架需要借鉴适合家庭使用的产品级安全标准。

政府的下一步行动

显然，插电式电池可能会给英国家庭带来变革，因为迄今为止，英国家庭仍无法享受家用电池带来的好处。 政府宣布推出插电式太阳能是积极的，但它却将插电式电池置于灰色地带。

Regen 建议 DESNZ 现在应该：

  • 承诺插入式电池在英国合法使用的日期
  • 委托对插入式电池进行快速安全研究，并与 IET 和 BSI 合作相应更新 BS 7671（英国接线法规）
  • 通过 BSI 赞助便携式家用设备电池防火安全的新产品安全标准（与为安装系统编写的 PAS 63100 框架不同）。

由于政府承诺从家庭能源账单中削减 300 英镑看起来越来越遥不可及，因此向市场推出一种新产品，无需财政部承担任何费用即可节省大量账单，这应该是更容易做出的决定之一。
